panel.title: LLM server
panel.viaSshTitle: This engine's port is not reachable from the dashboard, so it is read through an SSH tunnel to the unit
panel.notMeasuredTitle: The endpoint answered, but no rate could be measured on the last poll.
panel.decodeStrataTitle: Live sliding-window decode rate. When that window is unavailable, the active-slot mean sums each active slot’s generated tokens divided by its elapsed time since first token; it excludes prefill time.
panel.perStreamTensorFoldTitle: Completed-request decode rate (1 / mean per-request time per output token). Held between completions; not the speed of a currently running stream.
panel.perStreamTitle: Average decode throughput of one running stream (1 / mean seconds per output token). Only engines that publish a per-token latency histogram report it.
panel.prefillStrataTitle: Engine-reported mean for computed/new prompt tokens. It may be from an earlier prefill and is not an aggregate across slots.
panel.prefillTensorFoldTitle: Prompt tokens computed per second of prefill time (the engine's prefill-time and cached-token counters, finished requests only), held between completions. Tokens restored from the prompt cache are not counted here; they are the Cached prefill rate.
panel.prefillTitle: Prompt tokens/sec taken in during the last poll window — cache-served + computed. Opening a saved chat in the UI does not hit the GPU; send (or regenerate) so the history is sent as the prompt. Cached prefill does little GPU work; uncached prefill is what builds KV cache.
panel.prefillingStrataTitle: A prompt is being processed; no current prefill rate is available.
panel.prefillingTitle: A prompt is being processed. The engine reports its speed only when the request finishes.
panel.noPrefillMeasurementTitle: No current prefill measurement; zero is not evidence that no prompt is being processed.
panel.effectiveRateTitle: Token and prefill-time deltas over requests that finished in the same window; not continuous live throughput.
panel.cachedPrefillTitle: Prefill tokens served from prefix cache (little GPU work). High values mean prompt reuse, not a faster cold prefill.
panel.uncachedPrefillTitle: Uncached (computed) prefill — tokens that actually build KV cache on the GPU.
panel.engineInfo: Active = processing or ready for requests. Sleeping = idle, GPU memory freed until next request.

metricInfo.kvCache: Free tokens left in the engine’s KV-cache pool, over the allocated pool (tokens and memory). The pool is shared across concurrent requests and can be larger than one request’s max context. High usage (≥80% full) means little room for new or long contexts and often leads to queuing or preemptions.
metricInfo.requests: Run = requests actively generating on the GPU. Wait = accepted but not yet scheduled (capacity or constraints). Growing wait with high KV cache usually means the server is overloaded.
metricInfo.ttftMean: Mean time-to-first-token reported by FreeToken (a mean, not a percentile): how long requests wait until the first output token.
metricInfo.ttftP95: 95th percentile time-to-first-token from the engine’s request history: how long “slow” requests wait until the first output token. Spikes mean queueing, long prefills, or cold paths—not average decode speed.
metricInfo.preempts: Cumulative times the engine paused a running request to free KV cache for others. Rising under load signals memory pressure; zero is normal when the server is comfortable.
metricInfo.prefixCache: Lifetime fraction of prefix-cache lookups that hit (hits ÷ queries). Higher means more prompt reuse and less prefill work; — when the series is missing or unused.
metricInfo.e2eP95: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency from the engine’s request history: arrival until the request finishes. Includes queue wait, prefill, and decode—not just token generation speed.
metricInfo.itlP95: 95th percentile inter-token latency (time between successive output tokens) from the engine’s request history. Spikes mean decode stalls or contention; lower is smoother streaming.
metricInfo.mtpAccept: Lifetime speculative / MTP acceptance rate (accepted draft tokens ÷ drafted tokens). Higher means speculative decoding is paying off; — when speculation is off or unused.
